mechanism_narrative: The current federal funds rate level (FEDFUNDS) is inversely related to S&P 500 forward returns, such that higher FEDFUNDS consistently produces negative 20-day returns for the S&P 500 due to compressed equity valuations from elevated discount rates.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS exceeds 4.0%.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) exceeding 0.3 percentage points over a 3-month period signals deteriorating labor market conditions, triggering negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE has increased by more than 0.3pp over the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) exceeding 0.5% in one month indicates weakening consumer demand, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST and RSAFS both decline > 0.5% in 1 month
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when both HOUST and RSAFS decline by more than 0.5% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of strong industrial production growth (INDPRO > 0.5% quarterly), the economy is in late-cycle expansion, which is associated with negative S&P 500 forward returns due to overvaluation and impending policy tightening.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when INDPRO growth rate exceeds 0.5% in the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A decline in housing starts (HOUST) below 2000.0 thousand units in the prior month signals a contraction in the housing market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when HOUST falls below 2000.0 in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: A combination of high federal funds rates (FEDFUNDS > 4.0%) and accelerating inflation (CPIAUCSL increase > 0.2% monthly) signals a monetary tightening cycle, which produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2% in 1 month
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 20-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when FEDFUNDS > 4.0% and CPIAUCSL rises > 0.2% in the prior month.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high unemployment (UNRATE > 5.0%) and weak job growth (PAYEMS growth < 0.2% in 3 months), the labor market is slack, signaling economic weakness and leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS growth < 0.2% in 3 months
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 60-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when UNRATE > 5.0% and PAYEMS growth < 0.2% in the prior 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly acceleration in the CPI (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.3% signals rising inflation, which triggers negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days due to immediate market reaction.
failure_condition: The S&P 500 produces positive 5-day forward returns in more than 60% of instances when CPIAUCSL rises > 0.3% in the prior month.
